prompt:
Review the contingency case status and the journal entry register, together with relevant documents, and propose a journal entry where applicable for all relevant transactions. If entries have already been posted into the QBO journal entry register 2024 document, do not propose a journal entry.

For all of the above, focus on the settled case.

Provide answers in the console, present amounts in $, and round numeric data to the nearest whole number, but do not round intermediate values.
criteria: Proposes the journal entry for Whitfield post-settlement holdback as $29,700 Dr Contingency Fee Revenue (or Account 4200), Cr Accrued Expenses (or Account 2050) (acceptable value is $29,700)
States exactly one FY2024 journal entry in total, with interest excluded.

runs.answer:
**Whitfield (M-2024-0018): what needs a journal entry**

**1. Settlement receipt on 12/15/2024: no entry proposed.**
The 2024 JE register already has both wires:
- JE-OB-000842: Dr 1000 Operating Checking $594,000 / Cr 4200 Contingency Fee Revenue $594,000.
- JE-OB-000843: Dr 1000 Operating Checking $45,000 / Cr 1300 Client Cost Advances $45,000.

These match the settlement summary and the case status report. The $1,161,000 net to the client was wired administrator-to-trustee and never touched Sterling's books or IOLTA, so nothing is needed for it. Meadowbrook and Ferndale are unsettled, so I did not propose entries for them.

**2. Competing-claim holdback and fee return: entry proposed, because the register has nothing for it.**
- The competing claim was filed in late November 2024. Its facts therefore existed at 12/31/2024, even though the administrator's notice only arrived on 1/9/2025. I treated it as a recognized subsequent event and booked it in 2024.
- The $90,000 holdback reduces the gross used for the fee calculation. Adjusted gross is $1,710,000, so the fee entitlement is $564,300 at 33%.
- The fee already received was $594,000, so the excess to return is **$29,700**. That is 33% × $90,000.
- The cost reimbursement wire is not recallable, so there is no entry for it.
- The $29,700 is a fee return, which is a reversal of revenue. It is not an expense.
- No chart-of-accounts account fits the liability well. I used 2050 Accrued Expenses, but a dedicated "Refund liability – settlement administrator" account would be cleaner.

| Date | Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12/31/2024 | 4200 Contingency Fee Revenue | 29,700 | |
| 12/31/2024 | 2050 Accrued Expenses (refund liability to settlement administrator) | | 29,700 |

**3. Interest on the excess disbursement: entry proposed, because the register has nothing for it.**
- The January 10, 2025 grace deadline was missed, so interest runs from 12/15/2024 on the full $29,700 at 5% per year, accruing daily.
- Accrued through 12/31/2024 is 16 days (12/15 to 12/31), and 2024 is a leap year, so I used 366 days.
- $29,700 × 5% × 16/366 = $64.92, which rounds to **$65**.
- On a 365-day basis it is $65.10, which also rounds to $65.
- The chart of accounts has no interest expense account (only 8000 Interest Income). I used 6950 Bank Fees as the nearest fit, but you may want to add a dedicated interest expense account.
- Interest keeps accruing in 2025 until the funds are returned. That is about $4.06 per day, and it is a 2025 expense. If the return date is known, the final amount will be higher.

| Date | Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12/31/2024 | 6950 Bank Fees (interest expense – use a dedicated account if added) | 65 | |
| 12/31/2024 | 2050 Accrued Expenses (interest payable to settlement administrator) | | 65 |

**Net effect on 2024:**
- Contingency fee revenue goes from $594,000 to $564,300.
- Accrued liabilities rise by $29,765.
- Pre-tax income falls by $29,765.

**Follow-up:** The $90,000 holdback itself sits in the administrator's escrow, so Sterling has no entry for it. If the competing claim is resolved in the firm's favor in Q1 2025, the $29,700 fee would be re-recognized then.

runs.answer:
## Whitfield (M-2024-0018): proposed entries

**Already posted, so no entry proposed.** The settlement receipts are in the 2024 JE register:
- JE-OB-000842 (12/15/2024) is Dr 1000 Operating Checking $594,000 and Cr 4200 Contingency Fee Revenue $594,000.
- JE-OB-000843 (12/15/2024) is Dr 1000 Operating Checking $45,000 and Cr 1300 Client Cost Advances $45,000.

The $1,161,000 net to the client went from the administrator straight to the trustee. It never touched Sterling's books or IOLTA, so no entry is needed for it.

**Not posted, so I propose two entries.** The register has no entry for the $90,000 holdback clawback or for the interest. The Whitfield 1/14/2025 memo says a competing claim was filed in late November 2024. That condition existed at 12/31/2024, so both items should be booked as year-end adjustments.

**Entry 1: fee clawback (12/31/2024)**

The administrator recalculated Sterling's fee on the adjusted gross, so the return falls entirely on the fee. The cost reimbursement wire is not recallable.

Return obligation = $90,000 × 33% = **$29,700**.

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| 4200 Contingency Fee Revenue | $29,700 | |
| 2050 Accrued Expenses (refund due to settlement administrator) | | $29,700 |

Fee revenue becomes $564,300, which is 33% × $1,710,000. There is no dedicated refund-liability account in the chart of accounts, so I used 2050. The cash has not yet been returned.

**Entry 2: interest on the excess disbursement (12/31/2024)**

The 1/10/2025 grace date was missed. Under §7.4, interest therefore runs from 12/15/2024 on the full $29,700 at 5%. I accrued it through 12/31, which is 16 days.

$29,700 × 5% × 16/365 = $65.10, or **$65** rounded. A 366-day year also gives $65.

| Account | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Interest expense (no account exists in the chart of accounts, so add one, e.g. 9100 Interest Expense) | $65 | |
| 2050 Accrued Expenses (interest payable to settlement administrator) | | $65 |

Interest continues to accrue in 2025 until the funds are returned. Book that when it happens.

**Effect at 12/31/2024:** revenue and pre-tax income fall by $29,765 in total. Liabilities rise by $29,765. When the $29,700 is returned in 2025, relieve 2050 against cash. Nothing further goes through revenue.

**Other contingency cases:** Meadowbrook (M-2024-0016) and Ferndale (M-2024-0017) are unsettled. No fee revenue is recognized for them under the firm's recognition policy, so no entry applies.

**Assumption to confirm:** the $29,700 uses the standard 33% pre-trial rate. I did not check the engagement letter, but the settlement summary cites 33% "per engagement letter."
